# Isaiah Chapter 49 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 154r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/ISA_049_page_001.jpg

---

**49:1** Listen [shimu] to-me, O-coastlands [iyyim], and-give-attention [veha-qeshivu], O-peoples [le'ummim] from-afar [me-rachoq]: YHWH from-the-womb [mi-beten] called-me [qera'ani]; from-the-body [mi-me'ei] of-my-mother [immi] he-named [hizkir] my-name.

**49:6** And-he-said, "It-is-too-light-a-thing [naqel] that you-should-be [mi-heyotkha] my-servant to-raise-up [le-haqim] the-tribes [shivtei] of-Yaakov and-the-preserved [netsurei] of-Yisra'el to-restore [lehashiv]; and-I-will-give-you [u-netattikha] as-a-light [le-or] of-the-nations [goyim], to-be my-salvation [yeshu'ati] to the-end [qetseh] of-the-earth [ha-arets]."

**49:15** "Can a-woman [ishah] forget [hatishkach] her-nursing-child [ulah], from-having-compassion [me-rachem] on-the-son [ben] of-her-womb [bitnah]? Even [gam] these may-forget [tishkachnah], but-I will-not forget-you [lo eshkachekh]."

**49:16** "Behold, on-the-palms [al-kappayim] of-my-hands I-have-engraved-you [chaqqotikh]; your-walls [chomotayikh] [are] before-me [negdi] continually [tamid]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1-6 — The Second Servant Song:** The Servant now speaks in the first person. His mission expands: not only to restore Israel but to be "a light to the nations" — salvation reaching "the end of the earth."

**v.15-16 — "Can a mother forget?":** One of the most intimate divine self-descriptions in Scripture. God's love for Israel exceeds even a mother's love for her nursing child. "I have engraved you on the palms of my hands" — Israel's name is permanently inscribed on God.

*— EMET*
